messages:
kevin: Heads up — seeing a ~12% drop in daily `api_request_counts` for hosted routes starting 2026-02-14 01:00 UTC. Numbers in the console disagree with raw events. :eyes:
anya: Do we have sample late events or an error spike from the router?
kevin: Found a batch of events arriving with `ingest_timestamp` ~40m after `event_time`. Some have missing `route_id`. pasted one below:
```
{"event_time":"2026-02-14T00:42:12Z","ingest_timestamp":"2026-02-14T01:22:31Z","client_id":"abc","route":"/v1/generate","status":200}
```
sam: Two ways to fix: 1) streaming replay: read raw topic offsets and re-hydrate aggregates (near real-time), or 2) batch recompute: run parquet/history aggregate job to produce corrected counts. Streaming can be faster but messier for dedupe.
maria: If we replay into the same pipeline we risk double counting unless we use idempotent keys or tombstones. Also quota/cost impact if we reingest everything.
telemetry-bot: ingest-lag alert (telemetry.events) fired 2026-02-14T01:30:05Z, lag=~35m, open incidents/telemetry/435
kevin: My preference is batch recompute for this window only (00:30–01:30 UTC) and then a small streaming fix if there are still tails. Batch gives auditable aggregates.
sam: Agreed. Proposed plan:
- snapshot raw offsets for the time window
- run pyspark job against S3 parquet to recompute per-route aggregates
- write results to `telemetry.recompute.v1` topic with `recompute_window` metadata
- run merge job that upserts aggregated counts into the materialized table (idempotent)

Example spark command:
```
spark-submit --conf spark.executor.memory=12G jobs/recompute_telemetry.py \
  --start 2026-02-14T00:30:00Z --end 2026-02-14T01:30:00Z --out s3://redwood-telemetry/recompute/20260214/
```
anya: We need schema validation step. Some old events missing `route_id` — do we backfill `route` by heuristics? That could alter counts.
maria: Don't backfill heuristically for production tallies. If route missing, mark as `route:unknown` and surface percentage in dashboard.
julian: I can add a temporary pane in Console to show pre/post recompute diff with a toggle. @julian will need `recompute_window` tag on outputs.
infra-oncall: Off-peak compute window tonight UTC 03:00–05:00 looks free. Large Spark runs OK but notify infra 30m before job. Also watch S3 request rates (we throttle).
kevin: Action items:
- @maria: confirm schema rules for unknown/missing fields (today EOD)
- @sam: prepare recompute job and dry-run on a 10% slice (tomorrow morning)
- @julian: add console diff pane (flagged)
- @infra-oncall: reserve cluster slot for 03:00–05:00 UTC and confirm S3 throttle settings
- @anya: produce quick runbook for the merge/upsert step (idempotency notes)

maria: Will validate and post schema decision in the thread. If we mark `route:unknown`, also include `missing_route_pct` in metadata.
sam: I'll push a dry-run artifact with metrics to `gs://redwood-test/recompute-dryrun/1769500001/` and link here when ready.
kevin: Nice. Let's aim to run the full recompute tonight if dry-run looks good. Ping me when dry-run complete. :thumbsup:
telemetry-bot: automation-note: created task telemetry/recompute/1769500001 assigned to @sam
anya: Thanks — this approach avoids a risky streaming replay. We'll iterate if tails persist.
kevin: Closing loop: after merge, we'll run QA checks: compare per-route diffs, total token counts, and customer-impact queries (top 10 customers). Report back in this thread.
